dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: You come from a faraway place. How about lighting a Crane Crown Incense for good luck?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Crane Crown Incense"?

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: Look, there's a stone hanging over the cliff of the Yilong Dais, like the head of a crane.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: If you light one at the censer there, the adepti will hear your wish. Works every time, trust me on that!

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: The trip to the crane's head isn't for the faint-hearted, though. Many guests lost their composure as soon as they looked down.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: That's why we now have a proxy service.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: It'll cost you the equivalent of two cups of tea, but you get a wish that'll come true. Not a bad deal, right?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You are?

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: I'm the owner of this tea stall, and I'm also in charge of cleaning the Yilong Dais daily.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: This place used to be full of tourists. I took over this job from my master almost twenty years ago, and I've lit the Crane Crown Incense for countless guests.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: Whether it was the popularity of this place causing all sorts of paintings and photos to circulate, or maybe too many people had heard of or seen this place for themselves already...

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: But either way, it's not as appealing as before. Things haven't been as busy as it was years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: But times change. No point crying over that.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: I plan to recruit an apprentice, so they can carry this tradition forward.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: Then I want to make time to find several writers to write about the Yilong Dais, and promote our stories.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: For all I know, more people might realize that coming to the Yilong Dais to light a Crane Crown Incense will really make their wishes come true.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not right now, thanks though!

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: Farewell! If you want to make a wish, come find me or my future apprentice anytime!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do the people of Chenyu Vale also believe in the Crane Adepti?

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: Good question! I once had the same doubts, which I asked my master about.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: He just said that all adepti who can protect the people are good adepti, whether they be Carp, Crane, or Deer.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: So I stopped thinking about it. After all, they're just legends. No one knows if they're real or fabricated.

dialogues.speaker: Pingshan
dialogues.text: But if sincerity brings good luck, then that's all that matters!
